predecessors.name: Achaemenid Empire
predecessors.text: the Hebrus (Maritsa) valley within Cliopatria's -450 shape — Teres I's Odrysian heartland

successors.name: Tylis
successors.text: Seuthes III's realm around Seuthopolis in the Kazanlak valley and the Stara Zagora plain — 'ruled only part of Thrace'

ledger.x: c. 480; Teres I '480/450–430' in the king list, '460–445' on his own page, 'around 465' on the Skudra page. Founded in the Hebrus valley as Persian power in Europe collapsed; confidence 1 for the year.

Undated: Teres 'united the 40 or more Thracian tribes under one banner'; by Sitalces (431–424) the realm ran 'from Abdera in the south to the mouths of the Danube in the north' and 'from the Black Sea in the east to the sources of the Struma in the west'.
363–360: Cotys' general Miltokythes 'sent … into the Thracian Chersonese to take Sestos' (363/362); 'By 360 BC, Cotys controlled almost all of the Chersonese peninsula'.

September 360: Cotys I murdered; Cersobleptes succeeds and by 357 accepts Berisades (west, Maroneia–Strymon) and Amadocus II (centre, Maroneia–Maritsa) as 'autonomous rulers of parts of Thrace', keeping the land 'east of the Tonzos and Hebrus rivers' — the tripartite Odrysian kingdom.
357: the Chersonese 'seems to have been finally ceded to the Athenians in 357 BC', settled by Athenian cleruchs in 353.
352: Philip 'invaded as an ally of Perinthus and Byzantium'; Cersobleptes 'was defeated and sent one of his sons to Philip's court at Pella as a hostage'.

347: 'Philip advanced to the conquest of the eastern districts about Hebrus, and compelled the submission of the Thracian prince Cersobleptes'; the western king Cetriporis disappears in 347 and the Athenian coastal garrisons were expelled in 347/346.
342: Philip's 'larger campaign' of 342–340 against Cersobleptes and Teres III ends the tributary relationship in war.
342: Teres III's central kingdom falls — 'In 342 BC, Philip led a military expedition north' and renamed Eumolpia Philippopolis; Teres III's reign ends in 342 in the king list.
341–340: 'By early 341 he had overrun the coast and taken Cabyle'; Cersobleptes and Teres III 'eliminated or subjugated'; infobox 'Conquest by Philip II 340 BC'.
340: 'Inland Thrace was put under the loose control of a Strategos', with local rulers paying tithes — the Odrysian princes continue as Macedonian tributaries in the interior.
c. 325: Seuthes III 'revolted in about 325 BC, after Alexander's governor Zopyrion was killed in battle against the Getae'.
c. 325: Seuthes III's realm as drawn (60 km on Kazanlak); he 'ruled only part of Thrace' — Cabyle stayed with Spartocus, the coast with Lysimachus. Confidence 1 for the extent.
322: Seuthes with '8,000 cavalry and 20,000 infantry' and Lysimachus 'fought each other to a draw'.
After 322 Seuthes 'settled for peace' and 'appears to have acknowledged the overarching authority of Lysimachus' (year of the settlement not given; placed the year after the battle).
From c. 321: Seuthes 'acknowledged the overarching authority of Lysimachus', the strategos (from 306/305 king) of Thrace.
c. 320: 'Perhaps around 320 BC, Seuthes III established his residence at Seuthopolis' on the Tonzos near Kazanlak (founded 'between 325–315 BC').
313: Seuthes 'supported Callatis's revolt against Lysimachus', occupying the passes of Mount Haemus; the allies were defeated.
313–312: defeat and renewed submission; narrative sources stop mentioning Seuthes after 313–312, though coins suggest he ruled to 297.
281: Lysimachus 'at the decisive Battle of Corupedium was killed' in February 281; Thrace fell to Ptolemy Keraunos and then to the Celts.
281: Seuthopolis 'In 281 BC it was sacked by Celts'; Comontorius' Celts 'founded a kingdom in eastern Thrace centered around Tylis' c.

wars.name: Sitalces' invasion of Macedonia
wars.outcome: Sitalces, allied with Athens, invaded 'with a vast army that included 150,000 warriors' and withdrew for want of supplies; no territorial change.

wars.name: Chersonese war of Cotys I
wars.outcome: Cotys took Sestos (363/362) and 'almost all of the Chersonese' by 360; after his murder Cersobleptes ceded the peninsula to Athens in 357.

wars.name: Philip II's Thracian wars
wars.outcome: 'Conquest by Philip II 340 BC': the three Odrysian kingdoms absorbed, Philippopolis and Cabyle founded, inland Thrace 'under the loose control of a Strategos'; the sieges of Perinthus (340) and Byzantium (339) failed.

wars.name: Seuthes III against Lysimachus
wars.outcome: A draw in 322, defeat in 313; Seuthes 'acknowledged the overarching authority of Lysimachus' and kept his inland realm.

wars.name: Celtic invasion of Thrace
wars.outcome: Seuthopolis sacked (281); the Celtic kingdom of Tylis founded c.

certainty.note: Teres I's dates (480/465/460) and extent are disputed; drawn as the Hebrus valley.
Sitalces' realm is described by rivers and seas but no border is dated; Cliopatria's shape is accepted as the frame.
Partition and conquest are dated year by year on three pages; the internal lines (Tonzos–Hebrus, Maroneia) are approximate.
The tributary rump of 340–325 and Seuthes III's realm have no described borders; drawn as circles on the Kazanlak valley.
